title: Establish SDK demand signal catalog and triage heuristics for enterprise bindings
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Scope: Create a repeatable catalog of demand signals (qualitative + quantitative) to drive prioritization of SDK / client-library work for enterprise customers. Focus areas: language coverage gaps, authentication patterns (SSO/SAML, token rotation, KMS integration), and streaming ergonomics (resumable streams, backpressure, client-side SDK helpers).

Goals:
- Define a taxonomy of signals (sales requests, active customer blockers, support tickets, telemetry usage, OSS community + GitHub stars, implementation complexity, revenue impact).
- Produce a scoring rubric that converts signals into triage outcomes: Fast-track (concierge + SLA), Prioritized Backlog, Standard Backlog, Defer/Reject.
- Deliver a playbook and Linear intake automation to surface ranked SDK requests to PM + Eng leads on a weekly cadence.

Deliverables:
1) Signal catalog (CSV/Confluence) with definitions and example pulls.
2) Scoring rubric and example calculations for 10 historical requests.
3) Updated Linear intake template + labels mapping.
4) Runbook describing when to open Concierge tracks for high-ACV customers.

Rationale: Engineering capacity for SDKs is limited. Current intake is noisy (ad-hoc requests across Sales, Support, Solutions). A signal-driven approach will reduce manual prioritization overhead and align trade-offs (cost to build vs. revenue/retention).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Catalog published in Confluence and linked from intake form.
2) Scoring rubric validated with 2 PMs, 1 Sales AE, and Eng lead; examples executed for 10 historical requests.
3) Linear template updated (fields: customer_acv_bucket, impact_type, signals_checked, estimated_engineering_cost).
4) Playbook approved by Head of Product and Eng manager.
5) Demo to GTM + Support showing prioritized queue and expected outcomes.
decision_points:
- Thresholds for Fast-track vs Prioritized backlog (proposed: Fast-track if score >= 18 and customer ACV >= $100k/year OR customer_blocker=true).
- Whether to include OSS community metrics (GitHub stars) as a tiebreaker only.
- Support for multi-language request bundling (e.g., build core auth pattern once vs per-language bindings).
